extracted.intended_audience: Korean policymakers, central and local regulatory agencies, SME policy officials (SMBA, RRC, SMEs Ombudsman), and legislators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and recommendations for improving Korea's regulatory policy and governance, with a strong focus on ex post evaluation, SME-tailored regulation, regulatory impact analysis (RIA), and institutional arrangements to reduce burdens and improve regulatory quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey comparability and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparing survey data sets from different organisations may show low comparability because the methodology and design of each survey vary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using surveys to measure satisfaction or regulatory impacts, ensure consistent methodology and design across organisations to increase comparability; be cautious interpreting year-to-year changes if survey designs differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce ex post evaluation strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a strategy or system of ex post evaluation that looks at the overall impact of existing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a systematic strategy to assess the overall impact of existing regulations to improve the quality of regulatory performance assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish and discuss planned evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly discuss and publish planned evaluations to properly structure evaluation activities and improve transparency and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing planned evaluations ensures ex post analyses are well-planned, improves transparency, and prompts relevant stakeholders to participate in evaluation exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate quality control in regulatory reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality control systems should be integrated in regulatory reduction initiatives to avoid increasing regulatory burden when reducing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prevent 'less is more' problems, integrate quality-control checks so that abolished or reduced regulations contribute to overall regulatory improvement and have a positive effect on the sector or economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure regulatory quality with clear criteria and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measuring improvements in regulatory quality is essential through introducing clear and systematic criteria and developing metrics to show the added value of regulatory quality initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce explicit criteria to guarantee regulations meet intended objectives and develop metrics to measure both outcomes and the quality of regulatory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen evidence-based policymaking via KPIs and databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to strengthen initiatives that support evidence-based policy making through setting up a public database that monitors the development and outcomes of key performance indicators and constructing robust yet implementable evaluation methodologies for evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create publicly accessible KPI monitoring systems and adopt robust, implementable evaluation methodologies to underpin evidence-based regulatory reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: SME classification standards (sales- and employee-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2015, SMEs are classified by their average sales over the past three years with industry-specific sales ceilings; micro enterprises are defined by employee counts with sector-specific thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply industry-differentiated thresholds (sales ceilings or employee counts) consistently when defining SME/small/micro enterprise status, as this determines eligibility for tailored regulatory relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored Regulatory Approach and time-limited exemptions for micro enterprises
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tailored Regulatory Approach for SMEs (included in the Prime Minister's Ordinance) exempts micro enterprises with less than 10 full-time employees, in principle, from regulations for 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement time-limited, size-based exemptions (e.g., 3-year exemptions for qualifying micro enterprises) to reduce compliance burdens and support growth, while monitoring effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide SME-specific regulatory exemptions and simplified requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual laws have stipulated SME-tailored regulations (e.g., micro enterprises exempted from drafting employment rules; allowed to report salary totals in written rather than electronic form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use legislative and administrative instruments to provide lighter, more practicable obligations for SMEs (simplified reporting, exemptions) proportionate to enterprise capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of RIA on SMEs and public RIA statements (RIAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: RIA on SMEs produces RIA statements (RIAS) that are made public through the official gazette and various portals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure RIA findings for SME-relevant proposals are published and accessible (official gazette, agency websites, regulatory portals) to support stakeholder scrutiny and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mainstream RIA on SMEs into the general RIA process
rubrics_metrics.description: Streamline RIA on SMEs to the general RIA process to avoid duplications and pave the way towards more integrated policy development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate SME-focused RIA work (currently often done by SMBA) into the broader regulatory review process to reduce duplication and improve coherence across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate regulations according to enterprise size
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tailored Regulatory Approach differentiates regulations geared towards SMEs to balance burdens that are disproportionally imposed on SMEs vis-à-vis large conglomerates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design proportional and flexible regulatory alternatives that take account of enterprise size and characteristics to avoid imposing uniform burdens that disproportionately affect SMEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish independent SME advocacy and problem-identification bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: The SMEs Ombudsman (independent under SMBA) and the Public-Private Joint Regulation Advancement Initiative (PPJRAI) identify on-site regulatory difficulties, improve unreasonable regulations, and inspect the implementation progress of regulatory reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create or empower independent bodies (ombudsman, joint initiatives) to represent SME interests, identify practical regulatory problems, and monitor reform implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional regulatory petition centres and frequent stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory petition centres for SMEs have been set up in regional SMBA offices and local governments; the SMEs Ombudsman holds frequent meetings to address complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accessible, regionally distributed complaint and petition channels and maintain frequent engagement (regular meetings) to resolve SME regulatory issues promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a negative-list approach (permit unless prohibited)
rubrics_metrics.description: The negative list approach permits all business activities in principle unless prohibited by law (except health and safety), aiming to spark innovation and ease constraints for start-ups and emerging industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use negative-list regulatory frameworks to reduce unnecessary pre-approval restrictions and encourage experimentation and entry in emerging sectors, while retaining prohibitions for health/safety where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove 'thorn-under-the-fingernail' regulations systematically (RTUF)
rubrics_metrics.description: The RTUF initiative aims to remove regulations that are easily neglected yet impose significant impacts on business innovation and performance; stakeholders identify such regulations for removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement targeted programs to identify and eliminate small but impactful regulatory burdens, track the number of identified and reformed rules, and increase agency accountability for addressing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide SMEs grace periods to comply with new regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide SMEs with extra time or grace periods to comply with new regulations to help them adjust given their limited capacity and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer phased implementation timelines or temporary relief for SMEs when new requirements are introduced to incentivise compliance and innovation while minimising disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess annual regulatory policy impact on SMEs in RRC reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: During the annual reporting of the RRC, provide an assessment of the impact of regulatory policies on SMEs for each year’s regulatory activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include cumulative assessments in annual oversight reports to identify regulations that impose significant burdens on SMEs and those that support sectoral growth; use these assessments to prioritise reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate regulatory reform across central, local and legislative actors
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts to reduce regulatory burden have come from central agencies, local governments and the legislature; dispersed efforts can lead to redundant reforms and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhance coordination mechanisms across levels of government and with the legislature to avoid duplication, ensure complementary initiatives, and deliver integrated regulatory policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend regulatory review to parliamentary-initiated legislation to close governance gap
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation initiated by the National Assembly is not subject to compulsory regulatory review, creating a governance gap that weakens regulatory quality improvement efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply or develop procedures to subject parliamentary-initiated bills to regulatory review (or equivalent scrutiny) to ensure consistent quality standards across executive- and legislature-originated regulation.
